examples.en: Seolleongtang has to come with kkakdugi.
Kkakdugi is made by cutting radish into cubes.

examples.ko: 깍두기 국물이 너무 맛있어서 밥을 비볐어요.
examples.en: The kkakdugi juice was so good that I mixed it into my rice.
I want to eat doenjang stew with kimchi and kkakdugi.

examples.ko: 어머니가 담근 깍두기를 조금 나눠 주셨어요.
examples.en: My mother shared some of the kkakdugi she made.

examples.ko: 이 깍두기는 너무 시어서 못 먹겠어요.
examples.en: This kkakdugi is too sour for me to eat.

explain: 배추김치와 달리 무로 만든 김치예요. 설렁탕, 곰탕, 국밥 같은 국물 음식과 같이 나올 때가 많아요. '깍두기'는 모양 때문에 네모나게 썬 것을 가리키기도 해요.

phrases.example: 사람이 모자라서 막내는 깍두기로 끼워 줬어요.
phrases.en: We were short on players, so we let the youngest join in as a 'kkakdugi'.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아이들 놀이에서 나이가 어리거나 실력이 모자라서 어느 편에도 속하지 않고 양쪽에 끼는 사람을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: In children's games, it refers to a player who is too young or less skilled and joins in without belonging to a fixed team.

explain_en: Unlike cabbage kimchi, this kimchi is made from radish. It often comes with soup dishes such as seolleongtang, gomtang and gukbap. The word can also describe things cut into small cubes.

examples.en: I don't want to hate anyone.
Why do you hate that person so much?

examples.ko: 어릴 때는 엄마를 미워한 적도 있어요.
examples.en: When I was little, there were times I resented my mom.

examples.ko: 그 사람을 계속 미워하면 마음이 힘들어요.
examples.en: If you keep hating that person, your heart gets tired.
We had a fight, but I didn't stay angry at my friend for long.

examples.ko: 사람들이 그 배우를 미워할 이유가 없어요.
examples.en: People have no reason to hate that actor.

explain: '싫어하다'는 음식이나 물건에도 쓰지만 미워하다는 주로 사람에게 써요. 반대말은 '사랑하다'나 '좋아하다'예요. '미워하다'는 동사라서 '나는 그가 미워요'(형용사 '밉다')와 '나는 그를 미워해요'를 구분해야 해요.
explain_en: 싫어하다 can be used for food or things, but 미워하다 is mostly aimed at people. Its opposites are 사랑하다 and 좋아하다. Note the pair: 밉다 (adjective, 그가 미워요) versus 미워하다 (verb, 그를 미워해요).

examples.en: I eat bacon and eggs for breakfast.
I fried the bacon in a pan until crispy and ate it.

examples.ko: 샌드위치에 베이컨을 조금 더 넣어 주세요.
examples.en: Please put a little more bacon in the sandwich.

examples.ko: 베이컨은 원래 짠 편이라서 조금만 먹어요.
examples.en: Bacon is salty by nature, so I only eat a little.
There is a little bacon left in the fridge.
Shall we wrap potatoes in bacon and grill them?

explain: 한국 사람들은 고기를 구워 먹을 때 보통 삼겹살을 먹고, 베이컨은 샌드위치·햄버거·파스타에 넣는 서양식 재료로 생각해요. 삼겹살은 두껍게 썰어서 상추에 싸 먹는다는 점도 달라요.
explain_en: When Koreans grill meat to eat, they usually have 삼겹살 (pork belly), and bacon is thought of as a Western ingredient for sandwiches, burgers, and pasta. 삼겹살 is also cut thick and eaten wrapped in lettuce.

examples.en: I often eat almonds as a snack.
I heard almonds are good for your health.

examples.ko: 빵 위에 아몬드가 잔뜩 뿌려져 있어요.
examples.en: Plenty of almonds are sprinkled on top of the bread.
It was my first time trying almond milk.
My younger sibling has an almond allergy, so we're careful.

examples.ko: 마트에서 구운 아몬드를 한 봉지 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a bag of roasted almonds at the mart.

explain: '아몬드 우유', '아몬드 초콜릿'처럼 다른 말 앞에 붙여서 자주 써요. 땅콩, 호두와 함께 '견과류'라고 불러요. 알레르기가 있는 사람이 있어서 식당에서 '아몬드 들어갔어요?'라고 묻기도 해요.
explain_en: Used before other words, as in 아몬드 우유 (almond milk) and 아몬드 초콜릿. Together with 땅콩 and 호두 it is called 견과류 (nuts). Because of allergies, people may ask at a restaurant: 아몬드 들어갔어요?

examples.ko: 우리 동네는 밤에 혼자 걸어도 안전해요.
examples.en: My neighborhood is safe even if you walk alone at night.
It's a safe place for kids to play.
Please drive safely on snowy days.
This road is dark, so it isn't safe.
I hope the school my child attends is safe.

examples.ko: 이 자전거 헬멧은 가볍고 안전해서 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: This bike helmet is light and safe, so it's very popular.

explain: '안전하다'는 실제로 위험이 없는 것이고, '안심하다'는 마음이 놓이는 것이에요. 반대말은 '위험하다'예요. '안전한 곳', '안전하게 운전하세요'처럼 모양을 바꿔 자주 쓰고, 헤어질 때 '안전 운전하세요'라고 인사하기도 해요.
explain_en: '안전하다' means there is actually no danger, while '안심하다' is about feeling relieved. The opposite is '위험하다'. It is often used as '안전한 곳' (a safe place) or '안전하게' (safely), and people say '안전 운전하세요' as a parting wish to drivers.

p.n: 무사하다 describes a person who came through danger unharmed, not a place.

examples.ko: 우리 집 화장실에 양변기를 새로 설치했어요.
examples.en: We installed a new toilet in our bathroom.
The toilet got clogged, so I called a repairman.
Water keeps trickling in the toilet.
Clean the inside of the toilet thoroughly with a brush.

examples.ko: 옛날 집에는 양변기가 없는 곳도 많았어요.
examples.en: Many old houses didn't have a sit-down toilet.

examples.ko: 양변기에 휴지 말고 다른 건 버리지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't throw anything but toilet paper into the toilet.

explain: 앉아서 쓰는 서양식 변기를 말하고, '좌변기'라고도 해요. 옛날식 화장실의 쪼그려 앉는 변기와 구분할 때 쓰는 말이에요. 일상에서는 그냥 '변기'라고도 많이 해요.
explain_en: It refers to the Western-style sit-down toilet and is also called '좌변기'. It is used to tell it apart from old-style squat toilets. In daily life people also just say '변기'.

examples.en: This drink has zero calories.

examples.ko: 사고가 제로가 되도록 모두 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: Everyone has to be careful so that accidents drop to zero.
My confidence is zero before the test, so I'm worried.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 설탕이 제로인 음료도 팔아요.
examples.en: This shop also sells drinks with zero sugar.

examples.ko: 오늘 제 체력은 거의 제로에 가까워요.
examples.en: My energy today is close to zero.
One bottle of zero cola, please.

explain: 숫자 0을 읽을 때는 수학에서 '영', 전화번호에서 '공'이라고 하고 '제로'는 '아주 없다'는 느낌으로 말해요. '칼로리 제로', '자신감 제로', '제로 콜라'처럼 쓰는 경우가 많아요. 외래어라서 일상 대화에서 가볍고 재미있게 들려요.
explain_en: When reading the number 0, Koreans say '영' in math and '공' in phone numbers, while '제로' carries the feeling of 'absolutely none'. It's common in '칼로리 제로' (zero calories), '자신감 제로' (zero confidence), and '제로 콜라'. As a loanword it sounds light and playful in daily talk.

examples.en: Shall we have curry rice for dinner today?
I put lots of potatoes and carrots in the curry rice.
Kids like curry rice.

examples.ko: 카레라이스는 만들기 쉬워서 자주 해 먹어요.
examples.en: Curry rice is easy to make, so we often cook it.
The curry rice was so spicy that I drank milk.

examples.ko: 이 식당은 카레라이스 한 접시에 팔천 원이에요.
examples.en: At this restaurant, a plate of curry rice is eight thousand won.

explain: 밥 위에 카레를 얹거나 부어 먹는 음식이고, 줄여서 '카레'라고도 많이 말해요. 그냥 '카레'는 소스를 가리킬 때도 있어요. '카레라이스를 만들다/먹다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It's rice served with curry on top, and people often shorten it to '카레'. Plain '카레' can also mean just the sauce. Say '카레라이스를 만들다' (make) or '먹다' (eat).

examples.en: Most people in Brazil speak Portuguese.
Portuguese and Spanish are a little alike.

examples.ko: 포르투갈어 노래를 듣고 싶어서 배우기 시작했어요.
examples.en: I wanted to listen to Portuguese songs, so I started learning it.
For me, Portuguese pronunciation is hard but fun.

examples.ko: 친구가 포르투갈어로 인사하는 법을 알려 줬어요.
examples.en: My friend taught me how to greet in Portuguese.
I'm studying Portuguese because I'm going to Lisbon next year.

explain: 포르투갈어를 쓰는 나라는 포르투갈, 브라질, 앙골라 등이에요. 스페인어와 글자는 닮았지만 발음이 많이 달라서, 말로 들으면 다른 언어로 느껴져요.
explain_en: Portuguese is spoken in Portugal, Brazil, Angola and elsewhere. It looks like Spanish on paper, but the pronunciation differs a lot, so it sounds like a different language.

examples.en: How many siblings do you have in total?
I grew up alone without siblings.

examples.ko: 명절에 형제자매가 모두 할머니 댁에 모여요.
examples.en: On holidays all the siblings gather at Grandmother's house.
Siblings grow close through fighting with each other.
You have to write your siblings' names on the form.
Among my siblings, I'm the youngest.

explain: 한국어에는 '동생'이나 '형, 누나, 오빠, 언니'처럼 나이와 성별에 따라 부르는 말이 따로 있어요. 형제자매는 이걸 모두 합쳐서 부르는 말이에요. 몇 명인지 물을 때나 서류에 쓰고, 한 사람을 말할 때는 '동생이 있어요'처럼 구체적으로 말해요.
explain_en: Korean has separate words by age and gender: 동생, 형, 누나, 오빠, 언니. 형제자매 is the umbrella term for all of them. People use it to ask how many siblings someone has or on forms, and say specifics like 동생이 있어요 when talking about one person.

en: to put on make-up; to adorn oneself

examples.en: I put on make-up for ten minutes every morning.
I got up late today, so I didn't wear make-up.
My friend put on make-up nicely today.
I want to learn how to put on make-up.
I put on make-up and got dressed to go to the party.
I asked whether I may wear make-up at work.

explain: '화장하다'에는 소리가 같은 '화장(火葬)하다'도 있어서, 장례 이야기에서는 시신을 불에 태운다는 다른 뜻이에요. 얼굴 화장은 '메이크업하다'라고도 하고, 지울 때는 '화장을 지우다'라고 해요. '화장을 하다'처럼 띄어서도 많이 써요.
explain_en: '화장하다' has a sound-alike, '화장(火葬)하다', which in talk about funerals means cremation, so context matters. Face make-up is also called '메이크업하다', and removing it is '화장을 지우다'. People also often say it in two words, '화장을 하다'.
